title: Problem Header, Imports, and Namespace
content: File header documenting Erdos Problem #893 on the divisor sum of Mersenne numbers, status (OPEN, partially resolved by Kovac-Luca 2025), and references. Imports `Nat.Basic`, `Finset.Basic` for finite sums, `Real.Basic` for the ratio, `Filter.Basic` for limit concepts, and `Tactic`. Opens `Finset` namespace for sum notation and declares namespace `Erdos893`.
mathContext: Imports provide `Nat.divisors`, `Finset.sum`, `Finset.Icc`, $\mathbb{R}$ for ratios, and `Filter` for limit formulations.

title: Divisor Counting Function $\tau(n)$
content: Defines `tau n` as `n.divisors.card`: the number of positive divisors of $n$. This is the standard divisor function $\tau(n) = \sigma_0(n) = \sum_{d \mid n} 1$. For primes $p$, $\tau(p) = 2$; for prime powers $p^a$, $\tau(p^a) = a + 1$. The function is multiplicative: $\tau(mn) = \tau(m)\tau(n)$ when $\gcd(m,n) = 1$.

title: Verified $\tau$ Values for Small Mersenne Numbers
content: Proves $\tau(2^k - 1)$ for $k = 1, \ldots, 8$ using `native_decide`: $\tau(1) = 1$, $\tau(3) = 2$, $\tau(7) = 2$, $\tau(15) = 4$, $\tau(31) = 2$, $\tau(63) = 6$, $\tau(127) = 2$, $\tau(255) = 8$. The Mersenne primes ($3, 7, 31, 127$) have $\tau = 2$, while composite Mersenne numbers have more divisors. These verified values ground the abstract definitions in concrete computations.

title: Mersenne Primes Have $\tau = 2$ (Proved)
content: Proves `tau_prime_eq_two`: for any prime $p$, $\tau(p) = 2$. Uses `Nat.Prime.divisors` which gives $\{1, p\}$ as the divisor set of a prime. Applied to Mersenne primes $2^k - 1$, this shows they contribute minimally to $f(n)$.

title: Mersenne Divisor Sum $f(n)$
content: Defines `f n` as $\sum_{k \in \text{Icc}(1,n)} \tau(2^k - 1)$: the cumulative divisor count of the first $n$ Mersenne numbers $2^1 - 1, 2^2 - 1, \ldots, 2^n - 1$. Uses `Finset.Icc 1 n` for the summation range and `Finset.sum` ($\sum$) notation. The growth rate of $f$ is erratic because $\tau(2^k - 1)$ depends sensitively on the factorization of each Mersenne number.
mathContext: $f(n) = \sum_{k=1}^{n} \tau(2^k - 1)$. Growth depends on factorization structure of $\{2^k - 1\}_{k=1}^n$.

title: Verified Values of $f$ and Initial Values Theorem
content: Proves $f(1) = 1, f(2) = 3, f(3) = 5, f(4) = 9, f(5) = 11, f(6) = 17, f(7) = 19, f(8) = 27$ via `native_decide`, then collects them into `f_initial_values`. The jumps in $f$ reflect the divisor counts: Mersenne primes add 2, while composite $2^k - 1$ (like $k = 4, 6, 8$) add more. The ratio $f(8)/f(4) = 27/9 = 3$ gives early evidence for growth.

title: Monotonicity of $f$ (Proved)
content: Proves `f_mono`: $m \le n \implies f(m) \le f(n)$. The proof uses `Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset` with `Finset.Icc_subset_Icc_right`: extending the summation range can only add non-negative terms. This is a genuine Lean proof (no sorry, no native_decide), using the algebraic structure of finite sums.

title: Positivity of $f$ (Proved)
content: Proves `f_pos`: $1 \le n \implies 0 < f(n)$. The proof chains $0 < f(1) = 1$ (from `f_one`) with monotonicity $f(1) \le f(n)$ (from `f_mono`). This is needed to ensure the ratio $f(2n)/f(n)$ is well-defined (non-zero denominator).

title: Ratio $f(2n)/f(n)$
content: Defines `ratio n` as $(f(2n) : \mathbb{R}) / (f(n) : \mathbb{R})$, casting natural numbers to reals for division. This is the central quantity in Erdos's question. The ratio measures how much the divisor sum grows when the summation range doubles.

title: Ratio $\ge 1$ (Proved)
content: Proves `ratio_ge_one`: $1 \le n \implies 1 \le \text{ratio}(n)$. The proof uses `le_div_iff₀` (division characterization) and monotonicity $f(n) \le f(2n)$. This establishes that doubling the range never decreases the ratio. The proof is fully verified with no sorry.

title: Kovac-Luca: $\limsup f(2n)/f(n) = \infty$
content: Axiomatizes the main result of Kovac-Luca (2025, arXiv:2506.04883): for every $M > 0$, there exists $n$ with $\text{ratio}(n) > M$. This rules out any finite upper bound on the ratio but does not establish that the ratio eventually stays large (divergence). The proof builds on a heuristic argument by Cambie.

title: Ratio Unbounded (Proved from Axiom)
content: Proves `ratio_unbounded`: $\neg \exists B,\, \forall n,\, \text{ratio}(n) \le B$. The proof assumes a bound $B$ exists, applies `kovac_luca_limsup_infinite` with $\max(B, 1)$ to get a contradicting $n$, and derives a contradiction via `linarith`. This is a genuine proof (modulo the Kovac-Luca axiom) demonstrating formal reasoning with reals.
mathContext: $\neg \exists B \in \mathbb{R},\, \forall n,\, \frac{f(2n)}{f(n)} \le B$. Proof by contradiction using Kovac-Luca.

title: Erdos Problem #893: $f(2n)/f(n) \to \infty$
content: States the open problem as `ErdosProblem893`: for every $M > 0$, there exists $N_0$ such that $\text{ratio}(n) > M$ for all $n \ge N_0$. This is strictly stronger than the Kovac-Luca result: it requires the ratio to *eventually* exceed every bound, not just exceed it infinitely often. Defined as a `Prop` since the problem is open.

title: Conjecture Implies Kovac-Luca (Proved)
content: Proves `kovac_luca_weaker_than_conjecture`: `ErdosProblem893` implies the Kovac-Luca statement. The proof extracts $N_0$ from the conjecture and instantiates $n = N_0$ (using $N_0 \ge N_0$). This formally establishes the logical hierarchy: divergence (lim) is strictly stronger than unboundedness (limsup).
mathContext: $(\forall M,\, \exists N_0,\, \forall n \ge N_0,\, r(n) > M) \implies (\forall M,\, \exists n,\, r(n) > M)$

title: Summary Theorem
content: Collects the main verified results into `erdos893_summary`: positivity ($f(n) > 0$ for $n \ge 1$), monotonicity ($f$ is non-decreasing), and unboundedness of the ratio ($\neg \exists B,\, \forall n,\, \text{ratio}(n) \le B$). This serves as a machine-checkable summary of the formalization's achievements.
